number_of_offences: Number of offences/counts charged: 5; Number of offences finally upheld: 2
motive: Possessiveness due to suspicion of wife's infidelity
key_evidence_accepted: The prosecution successfully proved beyond reasonable doubt the incriminating circumstances against the accused, including the appellant's motive, the fire at the restaurant, the charred corpse identified as the deceased, blood-stained articles, and the appellant's possession of a revolver. The chain of circumstances pointed to the guilt of the appellant and established that he alone committed the murder and conspired with A2 to burn the body.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses' credibility by noting that the prosecution's case was based on circumstantial evidence and the credibility of the witnesses was supported by the chain of evidence pointing to the appellant's guilt. The court also noted that the appellant's behavior when shown the dead body suggested he was not remorseless.
post_offence_conduct: The appellant absconded after the offence but was eventually arrested and handed over to the Delhi Police. He was not remorseless as evidenced by his weeping when shown the dead body.
trial_duration: The prosecution case was that in the night intervening 2/7/1995 and 3/7/1995, the appellant killed his wife... The trial court convicted the appellant u/s. 302 IPC and also u/s.120-B r/w s.201 IPC and sentenced him to death. A2 was convicted u/s. 120-B r/w s. 201 IPC. The High Court confirmed the conviction and the death sentence awarded to the appellant.
legal_representation: Subramonium Prasad for the Appellant. Amarjit Singh Chandhiok, Mukul Gupta, Wasim A. Qadri, Ritesh Kumar, Shweta Gupta, Honey Kumari, Mallika Ahluwalia, Sadhna Sadhu, Anjali Chauhan, Zaid Ali, D. S. Mahra for the Respondent.
appeal_history: Trial court: Convicted and sentenced to death. High Court: Confirmed conviction and death sentence. Supreme Court: Commuted death sentence to life imprisonment.
prosecution_argument: The prosecution successfully proved beyond reasonable doubt the incriminating circumstances against the accused, including the motive (suspecting the deceased's fidelity and not wanting to make the marriage public), the murder, and the conspiracy with A2 to burn the dead body in the tandoor of the Bar-be-Que restaurant.
defence_argument: The appellant was not remorseless as evidenced by his weeping when shown the dead body, had no criminal antecedents, and the murder was the result of a strained personal relationship rather than an offence against society.
legal_principle_applied: The Court applied the principle of proportionality, the theory of reformation and rehabilitation, and the doctrine of the 'rarest of rare' cases, while considering aggravating and mitigating factors.
precedent_relied_upon: Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab, Smt. Triveniben v. State of Gujarat, and other cases cited in the judgment.
sentencing_rationale: The death sentence was commuted to life imprisonment due to mitigating factors such as the appellant's remorse, lack of criminal antecedents, and the fact that the murder was a result of a strained personal relationship rather than an offence against society.
judicial_mitigating_factors: The appellant was not remorseless, had no criminal antecedents, the murder was due to a strained personal relationship, and he was the only son of old and infirm parents who had spent over 10 years in death cell.
other_sentence_order: Life sentence for the whole of remaining life subject to remission granted by the appropriate Government under Section 432 CrPC, which is subject to procedural and substantive checks under Section 433-A CrPC.
